To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we present a simplified drift flux model (DFM), which is used in a UKF to estimate the unmeasured states and production parameters from the reservoir to the well.
the UKF is able to identify production parameters of gas from the formation and the slip parameters.
the UKF can be used to estimate the production constants of the gas phase and the slip parameters, and the UKF converges faster compared to EKF.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of a UKF based on a simplified DFM for estimating states and parameters of a multiphase flow during drilling.
the estimation of the unmeasured states and production parameters of the simplified DFM.
the development of the DFM, the design of a state estimator and the application of the state estimator in real time monitoring of drilling processes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the UKF performs better than EKF in the DFM, and that the proposed DFM can be used as a basis for a real time estimation of the production constants.
the UKF has a superior convergence rate, while the EKF is superior for the estimation of the slip parameters.
the proposed UKF is more accurate than the EKF for the estimation of unmeasurable states, production parameters, and slip parameters.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the proposed DFM with the UKF is capable of estimating the production constants of a well with reasonable accuracy, and the UKF has the ability to estimate states and parameters of the DFM.
the UKF is more accurate than the EKF for estimating the states and production constants of the DFM.
the proposed model and the UKF are promising for real time monitoring of multiphase flows during drilling.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the DFM is a viable model for real time estimation of states and parameters of multiphase flow in oil and gas wells.
the UKF is a promising method for real-time estimation and monitoring of the production and slip parameters of the multiphase flow.
the UKF is a viable alternative to EKF, which is more computationally expensive, for estimation of unobservable states and parameters.
